children.translated_text: The Veda is the root of <s>dharma</s>.
And so are the tradition and conduct of those who know it.
A transgression of <s>dharma</s>, and also recklessness, is observed among great men.
That is because of the weakness of those of lesser rank.
When authorities of equal strength conflict, there is optionality.
The upanayana of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is in the eighth year.
For a desired result, it may be in the ninth or the fifth.
The counting of the years begins from conception.
That is his second birth.
Therefore he is an ācārya, a teacher.
And also because he recites the Veda to him.
For a <s>kṣatriya</s> and a <s>vaiśya</s>, it is in the eleventh and twelfth years respectively.
Up to the sixteenth year, the Sāvitrī of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has not lapsed.
For a royal man, up to the twenty-second.
For a <s>vaiśya</s>, up to two years more than that.
The girdles, in order, are of muñja grass, bowstring, and thread.
The skins are those of the black antelope, the ruru deer, and the goat.
The garments for all are hempen cloth, linen, bark-cloth, and woolen cloth.
And unaltered cotton cloth.
Some also prescribe ochre-colored cloth.
For a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the garment is made from tree-bark fiber.
For the other two, it is dyed with madder and turmeric.
The staffs of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> are of bilva and palāśa wood.
For the remaining two, they are of aśvattha and pilu wood.
Or a sacrificially suitable wood may be used for all.
They should be uninjured, curved like a sacrificial post, and with the bark on.
They should measure up to the crown of the head, the forehead, and the tip of the nose respectively.
The hairstyles are shaven head, matted hair, topknot, and matted topknot.
When one is impure with something in the hand, one should set it down and perform ācāmana.
The purification of objects consists in wiping, burning, scraping, and washing, for things made of metal, gems, wood, and textiles respectively.
Stones, jewels, conch-shells, and pearls are treated like metal objects.
Bone and earth are treated like wood.
And earth is also purified by digging out and replacing it.
Rope, split bamboo, and leather are treated like cloth.
Things that are utterly damaged are to be discarded.
One should begin purification facing east or north.

children.text: śucau deśe āsīno dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ jānvantarākṛtvā yajñopavīty ā maṇibandhanāt pāṇī prakṣālya vāgyato hṛdayaspṛśas triś catur vāpa ācāmet ||
children.translated_text: Sitting in a clean place, placing the right arm between the knees, wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, washing the hands up to the wrist, restrained in speech, one should sip water touching the heart three or four times.
One wipes twice.
And one should sprinkle the feet.
One should also touch the openings in the head.
And one should place water on the crown of the head.
Again after sleeping, eating, and sneezing.
For things stuck to the teeth, the rule is as with the teeth, except when there is contact with the tongue.
Some say this applies before it has fallen out.
When they have fallen out, one should regard them like discharges; if one swallows them, that very thing is pure.

children.text: na mukhyā vipruṣa ucchiṣṭaṃ kurvanti na ced aṅge nipatanti ||
children.translated_text: Ordinary drops do not make one impure, provided they do not fall on a limb.
Purification from an impure substance consists in removing its smear and smell.
That is done first with water and then with earth.
And also in cases of contact with urine, feces, grease, bodily discharge, or food.
And wherever the sacred tradition prescribes it.

children.text: pāṇinā savyam upasaṃgṛhya anaṅguṣṭham adhīhi bho ityāmantrayed guruṃ tatracakṣurmanaḥprāṇopasparśanaṃ darbhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having grasped the left hand with the hand, excluding the thumb, he should address the teacher, saying, 'Recite, sir'; there the touching of eye, mind, and breath is done with darbha grass.
There are three breath-restraints, each of fifteen mātrās.
And the seat should be on grasses whose tips face east.
The syllable oṃ comes first, then the five vyāhṛtis ending with satya.
In the morning one grasps the guru's feet.
And at the beginning and end of Vedic recitation.

children.text: anujñāta upaviśet prāṅmukho dakṣiṇataḥ śiṣya udaṅmukho vā ||
children.translated_text: When permitted, the pupil should sit facing east on the teacher's right side, or facing north.
And there is recitation of the Sāvitrī.
At the beginning, when taking up the sacred utterance.
The syllable oṃ is used elsewhere too.
If one goes away in the interval, one must approach again.
After contact with a dog, ichneumon, snake, frog, or cat, there is a three-day fast and absence from study.
For the other cases, breath-restraints and eating ghee are prescribed.
The same applies to study near a cremation ground.
Before upanayana there is freedom to act as one wishes, speak as one wishes, and eat as one wishes,
from what has not been offered,
but the brahmacārin
becomes one who passes urine and feces as prescribed.
There is no fixed rule of ācāmana for him
apart from wiping, washing, and sprinkling.
There is no impurity from touching that.
But he should certainly not be appointed to fire-offering or the carrying of bali offerings.
Nor should one make him utter Vedic speech, except when pouring out an offering to the ancestors.
The discipline begins with upanayana.
Brahmacarya has been stated.
The tending of the fire and going for alms,
truthful speech,
and touching water are prescribed.
Some say it begins with the gift of a cow and the like.
And the twilight observance is to be performed outside.

children.text: tiṣṭhet pūrvām āsītottarāṃ sa jyotiṣy ā jyotiṣo darśanād vāgyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the earlier twilight he should stand, at the later he should sit, restrained in speech, until the light appears or until the stars are seen.
He should not gaze at the sun.

He should avoid honey, meat, perfumes, garlands, sleeping by day, anointing, riding in vehicles, shoes, umbrellas, desire, anger, greed, delusion, disputation, playing instruments, bathing, cleaning the teeth, merriment, dancing, singing, slander, and fear.
In the presence of the guru, he should avoid covering his neck, crossing his legs, leaning, and stretching out his feet.
He should avoid spitting, laughing, straddling, and slapping the body.
He should avoid looking at or touching women when there is suspicion of sexual intercourse.
He should avoid gambling, service to the low, taking what has not been given, and violence.
He should avoid uttering the names of the ācārya, his sons, his wife, and the initiated.
He should avoid impure or offensive words.
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should always avoid liquor.
He should sleep and sit lower, rise earlier, and go to rest later.
He should be restrained in speech, arms, and belly.
He should not indicate the guru's name and lineage as those of an equal.
The same applies when someone superior and honored is concerned.
Leaving his bed, seat, and place, he should answer when called.
At a command, he should approach even when not seen.
When serving someone placed lower or seated lower, and when seeing the guru, he should rise from a place exposed to cross-winds.
He should follow when the guru is going,
after announcing and reporting the task.
When summoned, he should study.
He should be intent on what is pleasing and beneficial.
And the same conduct applies toward the guru's wife and sons.
There should be no eating of leftovers, bathing, adorning, washing of the feet, massaging, or respectful salutation.
After returning from a journey, there is respectful salutation of the wives of the guru.
Some say this is not done to young women by one who has reached ordinary dealings with women.
Begging for alms may be done among all varṇas, excluding those who are accused or fallen.
At the beginning, middle, and end the word 'bhavat' should be used in the order of the varṇas.
If an ācārya, kinsman, or guru is not available, then elsewhere.
Among them he should avoid each earlier one in preference to the preceding.
Having informed the guru and been permitted, he should eat.
In his absence, he should inform the guru's wife, son, or fellow student.
Restrained in speech, becoming satisfied and not greedy, he should keep water nearby.
The correction of a pupil is to be without injury.
If he cannot do that, it may be with a thin rope or split bamboo.
If he strikes with anything else, he is to be punished by the king.
He should observe brahmacarya for twelve years for one Veda.
Or twelve years each for all of them.
Or until the learning is completed.
At the end of study the guru should be invited with a fee.
Or, when he has done so and has been permitted, there is the bath of completion.
The ācārya is the foremost of gurus; some say the mother is.
Some speak of an option regarding her āśrama.
The brahmacārin, the householder, the mendicant, and the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> are the āśramas.
Among these the householder is the source, because the others do not beget offspring.
There the rule for the brahmacārin has been stated.
Dependence on the ācārya lasts until the end.
After finishing the guru's work, he should recite.

children.text: gurvabhāve tadapatyavṛttis tadabhāve vṛddhe sabrahmacāriṇyagnau vā ||
children.translated_text: In the absence of the guru, he should live under the guru's offspring; in their absence, under an elder fellow student or by the sacred fire.
Living in this way, self-controlled, he attains the world of <s>Brahman</s>.
And for the later āśramas this applies insofar as it is not inconsistent.
A mendicant has no accumulation of property.
He keeps his semen raised upward.
During the rains he has a fixed mode of conduct.
Seeking alms, he should go to the village.
He should follow the lowest course, without turning back.
He should be one whose desires have turned away.
He is restrained in speech, sight, and action.
He should wear a garment for covering the loincloth.
Some say he should wear a discarded garment after washing it.
He should not take any part of herbs or trees that has not become detached.

children.text: na dvitīyām apartu rātriṃ grāme vaset ||
children.translated_text: Except in the rainy season, he should not stay a second night in a village.
He may be shaven-headed or have a topknot.
He should avoid the destruction of seeds.
He is equal toward beings with respect to injury and favor.
He undertakes no enterprise.
The <s>Vaikhānasa</s>, living in the forest, eating roots and fruits, is devoted to austerity.
He should establish the fire with the Śrāvaṇaka rite.
He eats no village food.
He honors gods, ancestors, humans, beings, and seers.
He is hospitable to every guest, except those who are forbidden.
He may use even what belongs to animals.
He should not stand on land ploughed with a ploughshare.
And he should not enter a village.
He wears matted hair and garments of bark and antelope skin.
He should not eat what is more than a year old.
But the teachers hold that there is only one āśrama, because there is direct prescription for the householder, for the householder.
A householder should marry a wife similar to himself, not previously given to another, and younger than himself.
Marriage is with those of different pravaras.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ saptamāt pitṛbandhubhyo bījinaś ca mātṛbandhubhyaḥ pañcamāt ||
children.translated_text: It should be beyond the seventh degree from the paternal relatives and beyond the fifth from the maternal relatives who share the seed.
The Brāhma marriage is when one gives a girl, clothed and adorned, to a man endowed with learning, conduct, family, and character.

children.text: saṃyogamantraḥ prājāpatye saha dharmaś caryatām iti ||
children.translated_text: In the Prājāpatya marriage the joining formula is, 'Let dharma be practiced together.'
In the Ārṣa marriage one should give a pair of cattle to the girl's father.
The Daiva marriage is the gift, after adorning her, to the officiating priest within the sacrificial enclosure.
Union by a willing woman herself is Gāndharva.
Purchase from those who have women, by means of wealth, is Āsura.
Because of forcible seizure, it is Rākṣasa.
Because of approaching one who is unaware, it is Paiśāca.
The first four are lawful.
Some say six are lawful.
In the direct, next, one-removed, and two-removed anuloma unions, the known offspring are Savarṇa, Ambaṣṭha, Ugra, Niṣāda, Dauṣmanta, and Pāraśava.
But in the pratiloma unions they are Sūta, Māgadha, Āyogava, Kṛta, Vaidehaka, and Caṇḍāla.
A Brāhmaṇa begets sons on women of the varṇas in order: Brāhmaṇa, Sūta, Māgadha, and Caṇḍāla.

children.text: tebhya eva kṣatriyā mūrdhāvasikthakṣatriyadhīvarapulkasāṃs tebhya eva vaiśyā bhṛjjakaṇṭhamāhiṣyavaiśyavaidehān pāraśavayavanakaraṇaśūdrān śūdretyeke ||
children.translated_text: From those same women a Kṣatriya begets Mūrdhāvasiktha, Kṣatriya, Dhīvara, and Pulkasa; from those same women a Vaiśya begets Bhṛjjakaṇṭha, Māhiṣya, Vaiśya, and Vaideha; a Śūdra begets Pāraśava, Yavana, Karaṇa, and Śūdra, according to some.
The teachers say that passing into another varṇa, by elevation or degradation, occurs in the seventh or fifth generation.
And this applies to those born in another creation or order.
But pratiloma offspring are without dharma.
And those born from a Śūdra woman are so too.
But from a Śūdra man with a woman not of the same varṇa there is the conduct of a fallen man.
The lowest is the most sinful.
Good sons purify.
Three ancestors are purified by a son from an Ārṣa marriage.
Ten are purified by a Daiva marriage and likewise ten by a Prājāpatya marriage.

children.text: daśa pūrvān daśa parān ātmānaṃ ca brāhmīputro brāhmīputraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The son of a Brāhma marriage purifies ten ancestors before him, ten descendants after him, and himself; the son of a Brāhma marriage.
He should approach his wife in her season.
Or at all times, except what is forbidden.
He honors gods, ancestors, humans, beings, and seers.
He performs daily Vedic recitation.
And he should give water to the ancestors, and other offerings according to his ability.
The wife is the beginning of the fire, or the inheritance is the beginning.
In that fire are the domestic rites.
The sacrifices to gods, ancestors, and humans, Vedic recitation, and the bali offering are to be performed.

children.text: agnāvagnir dhanvantarir viśve devāḥ prajāpatiḥ sviṣṭakṛd iti homaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The oblation in the fire is to Agni, Dhanvantari, the Viśve Devas, Prajāpati, and Sviṣṭakṛt.
And to the deities of the directions, each according to its place.
At the doors, offerings are made to the great ones.
On entering, to the household deities.
In the middle, to <s>Brahman</s>.
An offering should be tossed up into the air with the words 'to space.'
And in the evening to those who move by night.
After pronouncing a blessing, the gift of alms is made, preceded by water.
And thus also in righteous acts of giving.

The fruits are equal, double, thousandfold, and endless respectively when gifts are given to a non-Brahmin, a Brahmin, a <s>śrotriya</s> (Vedic scholar), and one who has reached the far shore of the Veda.
Prepared food is for those who beg; other things are for the others.
Even after promising, one should not give to a person joined with unrighteousness.
The words of one who is angry, delighted, frightened, distressed, greedy, a child, an old man, confused, intoxicated, or mad are untruths, but not sins causing loss of caste.
One should feed first the guest, the boy, the sick person, the pregnant woman, the woman dwelling in one's house, and the aged; the lowest should be fed last.
The act of cooking should be undertaken after informing the teacher, the father, and one's friends.
A <s>madhuparka</s> is offered at the arrival of an officiating priest, teacher, father-in-law, paternal uncle, or maternal uncle.
Again after a year.
But sooner on the occasions of a sacrifice or a wedding.
And also for a king and for a <s>śrotriya</s>.
For one who is not a <s>śrotriya</s>, a seat and water are given.

children.text: śrotriyasya tu pādyam arghyam annaviśeṣāṃś ca prakārayet ||
children.translated_text: But for a <s>śrotriya</s> one should arrange water for the feet, an <s>arghya</s> offering, and special kinds of food.
Or always food distinguished by proper preparation.
In the middle rank is the gift of food to a non-Vedic man who is of good conduct.
For those of the opposite character, grass, water, ground, a welcome, and, at the least, respectful worship and the avoidance of hostile expectation are to be given.
A bed, seat, lodging, escorting, and attendance are the same for equals and superiors.
Even a little is given to an inferior.
A guest is one from another village, staying one night, who has come at sunset and stands by a tree.
One should ask after the welfare, freedom from illness, and health of those who are well-disposed.
The last form is for a <s>Śūdra</s>.
For a Brahmin, a non-Brahmin is not a guest.
If, at a sacrifice, he is enclosed within the sacrificial precinct.
But a <s>Kṣatriya</s> is to eat after the Brahmins.
The others should be fed together with the servants, for the sake of compassion.
Taking hold of the feet should be done daily at a meeting.
And after approaching one who has been away.
This applies to one's mother and father, their relatives, elders, teachers of knowledge, and their teachers.
At an assembly, it is done to the superior.
In a gathering of those who know him, the greeting is to state one's own name and say, 'I am this person.'
Some say there is no fixed rule about greeting when women and men are together.
Women other than one's mother, paternal uncle's wife, wife, and sister are not greeted after one has not been away.
There is no grasping of the feet of brothers' wives or sisters.
But younger officiating priests, fathers-in-law, paternal uncles, and maternal uncles are to be honored by rising, and are to be greeted.
So too another earlier townsperson under eighty years old, even if a <s>Śūdra</s>, is treated like a child.
Even a lower <s>Ārya</s> is to be honored by a <s>Śūdra</s>.
Or one should avoid using his name.
A servant of the king who is not a reciter is also so treated.

children.text: bho bhavann iti vayasyaḥ samāne 'hani jātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One of the same age, born on the same day, is addressed as 'ho, sir.'

children.text: daśavarṣavṛddhaḥ pauraḥ pañcabhiḥ kalābharaḥ śrotriyaś cāraṇas tribhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: A townsman older by ten years, an artisan by five, and a <s>śrotriya</s> who is a Vedic reciter by three are to be honored as seniors.
Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and workers who are without learning are so classified by their occupation.
And an initiate before the purchase of the Soma.
Wealth, kinship, occupation, birth, learning, and age are grounds for honor, each following one being stronger than the preceding.
But sacred learning is weightier than all of them.
Because <s>dharma</s> and the Veda have that as their root.
The road is to be yielded to a cart-driver, a man in his tenth decade, one requiring favor, a bride, a <s>snātaka</s>, and a king.
But by the king it is to be yielded to a <s>śrotriya</s>.
In distress, a Brahmin may make use of learning from a non-Brahmin.
Following after him and service are required.
When the study is completed, the Brahmin is the teacher.
Sacrificing for others, teaching, and receiving gifts belong to all.
Each preceding one is the superior teacher.
Failing that, he may live by the occupation of a <s>Kṣatriya</s>.
Failing that, by the occupation of a <s>Vaiśya</s>.
The following are things not to be sold by him.
Perfumes, liquids, prepared food, sesame, hemp, linen, and skins.
Garments that are dyed or washed.
Milk together with its products.
Roots, fruits, flowers, medicines, honey, meat, grass, water, and harmful substances.
And animals when connected with slaughter.
Human beings, barren cows, unmarried girls, and injured animals are always forbidden.
Some also include land, rice, barley, goats and sheep, horses, bulls, cows, and draught oxen.
But there is a restriction.
Liquids may be exchanged for liquids.
And animals for animals.
But not salt or prepared food.
Nor sesame.
For immediate use, cooked food may be exchanged for an equal quantity of uncooked food.
When unable to live otherwise, one may maintain oneself in every way, provided it is not by a <s>Śūdra</s>'s occupation.
Some allow even that when life is in danger.
But the rule against mixture of caste and forbidden food remains.
When life is in danger, even a Brahmin may take up a weapon.
A <s>Rājanya</s> may take up the work of a <s>Vaiśya</s>.

children.text: dvau loke dhṛtavratau rājā brāhmaṇaś ca bahuśrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There are two in the world who hold firm vows: the king and the much-learned Brahmin.

children.text: tayoś caturvidhasya manuṣyajātasyāntaḥsaṃjñānāṃ calanapatanasarpaṇānām āyattaṃ jīvanam ||
children.translated_text: On them depends the life of the fourfold human race and of the beings called internal, those that move, fall, and creep.
Protection of offspring and the absence of mixture is <s>dharma</s>.
That same man becomes truly much-learned.
He knows the world, the Veda, and the auxiliaries of the Veda.
He is skilled in debate, <s>itihāsa</s>, and <s>purāṇa</s>.
He depends on that and lives by that.
He is purified by forty sacraments.
He is devoted to the three ritual acts.
Or to the six.
He is well trained in the customary rules of conduct.
By the king he is to be exempted in six respects.

children.text: avadhyaś cābandhyaś cādaṇḍyaś cābahiṣkāryaścāparivādyaś cāparihāryaś ceti ||
children.translated_text: He is not to be killed, not to be bound, not to be fined, not to be banished, not to be reviled, and not to be excluded.
The rites are conception, begetting a male child, parting the pregnant woman's hair, birth-rite, naming, first feeding of solid food, tonsure, and initiation.
The four Vedic vows.
The bath at completion of studentship and union with a wife who shares one's <s>dharma</s>.
The performance of the five sacrifices to gods, ancestors, humans, beings, and Brahmins.
And of these also.

children.text: aṣṭakā pārvaṇaḥ śrāddham śrāvaṇyāgrahāyaṇīcaitryāśvayujīti sapta pākayajñasaṃsthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>aṣṭakā</s>, the <s>pārvaṇa śrāddha</s>, the <s>śrāvaṇī</s>, <s>āgrahāyaṇī</s>, <s>caitrī</s>, and <s>āśvayujī</s> are the seven institutions of cooked offerings.

children.text: agnyādheyam agnihotraṃ darśapūrṇamāsāvāgrayaṇaṃ cāturmāsyāni nirūḍhapaśubandhaḥ sautrāmaṇīti saptahaviryajñasaṃsthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The fire-laying, the agnihotra, the new- and full-moon sacrifices, the first-fruits offering, the seasonal rites, the fixed animal sacrifice, and the sautrāmaṇī: these are the seven institutions of haviryajña.

children.text: agniṣṭomo 'tyagniṣṭoma ukthyaḥ ṣoḍaśī vājapeyo 'tirātro 'ptoryāma iti sapta somasaṃsthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The agniṣṭoma, atyagniṣṭoma, ukthya, ṣoḍaśin, vājapeya, atirātra, and aptoryāma: these are the seven soma institutions.
Thus these are the forty <s>saṃskāras</s> (sacraments).
Now, there are eight qualities of the self.

children.text: dayā sarvabhūteṣu kṣāntir anasūyā śaucam anāyāso maṅgalam akārpaṇyam aspṛheti ||
children.translated_text: Compassion toward all beings, patience, absence of envy, purity, freedom from strain, auspiciousness, absence of meanness, and freedom from craving.

children.text: yasyaite catvāriṃśatsaṃskārā na cāṣṭāv ātmaguṇā na sa brahmaṇaḥ sāyujyaṃ sālokyaṃ gacchati ||
children.translated_text: One who has these forty <s>saṃskāras</s>, but not the eight qualities of the self, does not attain union with <s>Brahman</s> or dwelling in the same world with it.

children.text: yasya tu khalu saṃskārāṇāmekadeśo 'py aṣṭāv ātmaguṇā atha sa brahmaṇaḥ sāyujyaṃ sālokyaṃ ca gacchati ||
children.translated_text: But one who has even a portion of the <s>saṃskāras</s> and the eight qualities of the self does attain union with <s>Brahman</s> and dwelling in the same world with it.

children.text: sa vidhipūrvakaṃ snātvā bhāryām adhigamyayathoktān gṛhasthadharmān prayuñjāna imāni vratāny anukarṣet ||
children.translated_text: Having bathed according to rule, taken a wife, and practiced the prescribed duties of a householder, he should continue these observances.
He is a <s>snātaka</s>.
He should always be pure, fragrant, and accustomed to bathing.
When he has the means, he should not wear old, dirty, or poor clothing.

children.text: na raktam ulbaṇam anyadhṛtaṃ vāso bibhṛyāt ||
children.translated_text: He should not wear red, gaudy, or previously worn clothing.
Nor garlands or shoes.
When unable, he may wear what has been washed.
He should not let his beard grow without reason.
He should not carry fire and water at the same time.
He should not drink from his cupped hands.
He should not sip water for purification while standing, with water drawn up.
Nor with water poured by a <s>Śūdra</s>, by an impure person, or with one hand.

children.text: na vāyvagniviprādityāpo devatā gāś ca pratipaśyan vā mūtrapurīṣāmedhyān vyudasyet ||
children.translated_text: He should not cast out urine, feces, or impurities while looking at wind, fire, a Brahmin, the sun, waters, deities, or cows, nor while facing them.
He should not stretch out his feet toward these deities.
He should not remove urine or feces with leaves, clods, or stones.
He should not step upon ashes, hair, nails, husks, potsherds, or impurities.
He should not converse with foreigners, impure persons, or unrighteous people.
After conversing with them, he should mentally meditate on those who do meritorious deeds.
Or he should converse with a Brahmin.
He should call a cow that is not milking 'one fit to become a milch cow.'
He should call what is inauspicious 'auspicious.'
He should call a skull a 'bhagāla.'
He should call a rainbow 'the jeweled bow,' not <s>Indra</s>'s bow.
He should not point out to another a cow that is suckling.
Nor should he stop her.
After sexual union, he should not delay purification.

children.text: na ca tasmin śayane svādhyāyam adhīyīta ||
children.translated_text: Nor should he recite his Vedic lesson on that bed.
And after studying in the latter part of the night, he should not lie down again.
He should not take pleasure in a woman who is not fit according to rule.
Nor in a menstruating woman.
Nor should he embrace her, nor a maiden.

He should avoid blowing into fire with his mouth, contentious speech, wearing garlands and perfumes outside, scratching himself before an inferior, eating together with his wife, looking at a woman applying collyrium, entering by a bad doorway, washing one foot with the other, eating while seated on a chair, crossing a river by the arms, climbing or descending a tree or uneven place, and risking his life.
He should not board a doubtful boat.
In every way, he should protect himself.
He should not wander by day with his head covered.
At night, he should have it covered.
And when urinating or defecating.
He should not do so on bare ground without interposing something.
Nor close to his dwelling.
Nor on ashes, dung, plowed ground, shade, a path, or a desirable place.

children.text: ubhe mūtrapurīṣe tu divā kuryād udaṅmukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By day he should urinate and defecate facing north.
And at the twilights.
At night, facing south.

children.text: pālāśam āsanaṃ pāduke dantadhāvanam iti ca varjayet ||
children.translated_text: He should avoid a seat, shoes, and tooth-cleaning stick made of palāśa wood.
With shoes on, and holding something in his hand, he should avoid taking a seat, greeting, and making obeisance.
He should not make the morning, midday, and afternoon fruitless, but, according to his ability, devote them to <s>dharma</s>, wealth, and desire.
Among these, however, <s>dharma</s> should be foremost.
He should not look at another man's wife when she is naked.
He should not pull a seat with his foot.
He should not indulge in fickleness of the penis, belly, hands, feet, speech, or eyes.
He should not, without cause, perform cutting, splitting, scratching, rubbing, or snapping.
He should not step over a calf's tether.
He should not go from family to family.
He should not go to a sacrifice uninvited.
But he may, if he wishes, for the sake of seeing it.
He should not eat food placed in his lap.
Nor food brought at night by servants.
He should not eat things whose potency has been taken away, such as what remains after clarified butter has been removed, gruel, oil-cake, or churned residue.

children.text: sāyaṃ prātas tvannam abhipūjitam anindan bhuñjīta ||
children.translated_text: In the evening and morning, he should eat food that has been honored, without disparaging it.
He should never sleep naked at night.
Nor bathe naked.

children.text: yac cātmavanto vṛddhāḥ samyagvinītādambhalobhamohaviyuktā vedavida ācakṣate tat samācaret ||
children.translated_text: Whatever self-possessed elders, properly disciplined, free from arrogance, greed, and delusion, and knowing the Veda, declare, that he should practice.
For security and prosperity, he should approach a ruler.
No other person, except gods, teachers, and righteous people.

children.text: prabhūtaidhodakayavasakuśamālyopaniṣkramaṇam āryajanabhūyiṣṭham analasasamṛddhaṃ dhārmikādhiṣṭhitaṃ niketanam āvasituṃ yateta ||
children.translated_text: He should strive to live in a dwelling that has abundant fuel, water, barley, kuśa grass, garlands, and exits, that is mostly inhabited by noble people, that is free from idleness and prosperous, and that is governed by a righteous man.
He should go around, keeping to the right, things that are praised and auspicious: shrines of deities and four-footed animals.

children.text: manasā vā tatsamagram ācāram anupālayed āpatkalpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, in an emergency, he should mentally observe that entire code of conduct.
He should be one whose rule is truth and <s>dharma</s>.
He should follow the conduct of the noble.
He should teach the well-trained.
He should be trained in purity.
He should be devoted to scripture.
He should always be non-injurious, gentle, firm in action, and habituated to restraint and giving.

children.text: evamācāro mātāpitarau pūrvāparāṃś ca sambandhānduritebhyo mokṣayiṣyan snātakaḥ śaśvadbrahmalokān na cyavate na cyavate ||
children.translated_text: Practicing such conduct, the <s>snātaka</s>, wishing to release his mother, father, and earlier and later relatives from evils, never falls away from the worlds of <s>Brahman</s>, never falls away.
For the twice-born, there are study, sacrifice, and giving.
For a Brahmin, teaching, officiating at sacrifice, and receiving gifts are additional.
But with respect to the preceding occupations there is a restriction.
Except in the cases stated, the handing over of Vedic knowledge is for a Brahmin under the rules concerning teacher, kinsman, dear person, elder, wealth, and learning.
Agriculture and trade are permitted, provided they are not carried on personally.
And money-lending too.
For the king, the additional duty is the protection of all beings.
And the use of punishment according to justice.
He should maintain learned Brahmins who are <s>śrotriyas</s>.
And Brahmins who are without means of exertion.
And he should make them free from taxes.
And those who are assisting him.
And effort should be directed toward victory.
Especially in danger.
And training with chariot and bow.
In battle there should be taking one's stand and not turning back.
There is no fault in violence in battle.

Except against those whose horses or charioteers are disabled, those without weapons, those with joined hands, those with loosened hair, those turned away, those sitting down, those standing on the ground, those climbed upon a tree, messengers, cows, Brahmins, and the like.

children.text: kṣatriyaś ced anyas tam upajīvet tadvṛttyā ||
children.translated_text: If a <s>Kṣatriya</s> has no other means, he may live by that occupation.
The conqueror should obtain the wealth won in battle.
But the vehicle belongs to the king.
And there is a special share when the victory is not separate.
The rest the king should distribute according to merit.

children.text: rājño balidānaṃ karṣakairdaśamam aṣṭamaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: The payment of tax to the king by cultivators is a tenth, an eighth, or a sixth.
Some say that for cattle and gold also the share is a fiftieth.
On merchandise the customs duty is a twentieth part.
Of roots, fruits, flowers, medicines, honey, meat, grass, and fuel, the sixth part is due.
Because he has the duty of protecting them.
But he should be constantly engaged with regard to them.
His livelihood is by the surplus.

children.text: śilpino māsi māsy ekaikaṃ karma kuryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Artisans should perform one piece of work each month.
By this, those who live by their own labor are explained.
And those who have boats and carts.
Food should be given to them.
Merchandise is to be supplied by merchants at a reduction of profit.
Having found something lost and without an owner, they should report it to the king.
After proclaiming it, it is to be guarded by the king for a year.
After that, a fourth belongs to the finder, and the remainder to the king.
Ownership arises in inheritance, purchase, division, acceptance, and finding.
For a Brahmin, what is obtained is additional.
For a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, what is conquered.
The finding of a treasure is royal property.
Except when it belongs to a worthy Brahmin.
Some say that even a non-Brahmin who reports it should receive a sixth.
Having recovered what was stolen by thieves, he should restore it to its proper place.
Or he should give it from the treasury.
The property of a child is to be protected until he reaches legal capacity.
Or until the completion of his studentship.
For a <s>Vaiśya</s>, agriculture, trade, cattle-keeping, and money-lending are additional.
The <s>Śūdra</s> is the fourth varṇa, of one birth.
For him too there are truthfulness, absence of anger, and purity.
Some say that for the purpose of sipping water, merely washing the hands and feet is sufficient.
And the rite of <s>śrāddha</s>.
The support of servants.
Living with his own wife.
And service to the higher varṇas.
From them he should seek his livelihood.
Among them, he should serve each earlier one before the next.
Worn-out shoes, umbrellas, garments, seats, and the like may be given to him.
And eating leftovers.
And livelihood by crafts.

children.text: yaṃ cāryam āśrayed bhartavyas tena kṣīṇo 'pi ||
children.translated_text: Whichever Ārya he takes refuge with must maintain him, even when he is reduced in means.
And by him the higher one is to be maintained.
His accumulation of property should be for that purpose.
When permitted, reverence is his mantra.
Some say that he may sacrifice for himself with cooked-offering sacrifices.
And all should serve the next higher in succession.
When the occupations of Ārya and non-Ārya are interchanged, there is equality of action.
The king has authority over everything, except Brahmins.
He should do good and speak in favor of good.
He should be trained in the three Vedas or in reasoning.
He should be pure, self-controlled, and furnished with worthy assistants and means.
He should be impartial toward his subjects.
He should do what is beneficial for them.

children.text: tam uparyāsīnam adhastād upāsīrann anye brāhmaṇebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he sits above, the others, except Brahmins, should sit below and attend upon him.
And they too should honor him.
He should protect the varṇas and āśramas according to justice.
And when they deviate, he should establish them in their own <s>dharma</s>.
For he becomes a sharer in a portion of <s>dharma</s>, so it is said.

children.text: brāhmaṇaṃ ca purodadhīta vidyābhijanavāgrūpavayaḥśīlasampannaṃ nyāyavṛttaṃ tapasvinam ||
children.translated_text: And he should place before himself a Brahmin domestic priest endowed with learning, noble birth, speech, appearance, age, and character, acting justly and practicing austerity.
With that priest's authorization he should perform actions.

children.text: brahmaprasūtaṃ hi kṣatram ṛdhyate na vyathata iti ca vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: For it is understood that royal power, when authorized by Brahman, prospers and is not shaken.
And whatever those who consider divine portents declare, he should heed.
For some declare prosperity and security to be dependent on that too.

In the household fire he should perform rites connected with pacification, auspicious days, blessings, long life, and good fortune for prosperity, and rites connected with creating hatred, subjugation, hostile magic, and the decline of enemies.
Other rites should be performed by the officiating priests as prescribed.

children.text: tasya ca vyavahāro vedo dharmaśāstrāṇy aṅgānyupavedāḥ purāṇam ||
children.translated_text: For him, the basis of legal procedure is the Veda, the <s>dharmaśāstras</s>, the auxiliaries, the subsidiary Vedas, and the <s>purāṇa</s>.
And the laws of region, caste, and family, when not opposed to the sacred traditions, are authoritative.
Cultivators, merchants, cattle-keepers, money-lenders, and artisans are authorities within their own respective class.
After ascertaining matters from them according to their competence, there is the settlement of <s>dharma</s>.
In the ascertainment of justice, reasoning is the means.
Having inferred by that means, he should bring the matter to its proper place.
When there is disagreement, after ascertaining from elders learned in the three Vedas, he should bring it to a conclusion.
For in that way his highest good comes about.
For it is understood that brahman joined with royal power upholds gods, ancestors, and human beings.
They say that punishment is so called from restraining; therefore by it one should restrain the unrestrained.

children.text: varṇāśramāḥ svasvadharmaniṣṭhāḥ pretya karmaphalamanubhūya tataḥ śeṣena viśiṣṭadeśajātikularūpāyuḥśrutacitravittasukhamedhaso janma pratipadyante ||
children.translated_text: The classes and life-stages, steadfast in their own respective <s>dharma</s>, after death experience the fruit of their actions and then, through what remains, obtain birth distinguished by place, caste, family, form, lifespan, learning, various wealth, happiness, and intelligence.
Those who turn away and act contrary to this perish.
The instruction of the teacher and punishment protect them.
Therefore the king and the teacher are not to be censured, not to be censured.

children.text: śūdro dvijātīn abhisaṃdhāyābhihatya cavāgdaṇḍapāruṣyābhyām aṅgamocyo yenopahanyāt ||
children.translated_text: If a <s>Śūdra</s>, intending harm toward twice-born men, strikes them or injures them with verbal or bodily violence, he is to be deprived of the limb with which he harmed them.
For intercourse with an <s>Ārya</s> woman, there is removal of the organ and confiscation of his property.
If she is under guardianship, the penalty is greater, death.

children.text: atha hāsya vedam upaśṛṇvatas trapujatubhyāṃ śrotrapratipūraṇam udāharaṇe jihvāchedo dhāraṇe śarīrabhedaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Further, if he listens to the Veda, his ears are to be filled with tin and lac; if he recites it, his tongue is to be cut out; if he retains it in memory, his body is to be split.
One who seeks equality in seat, bed, speech, or road is to be fined.
A <s>Kṣatriya</s> owes one hundred for insulting a Brahmin.
For bodily violence, twice as much.
A <s>Vaiśya</s> owes one and a half times that.
But a Brahmin owes fifty for insulting a <s>Kṣatriya</s>.
Half of that for insulting a <s>Vaiśya</s>.
For a <s>Śūdra</s>, nothing at all.
The rule for a <s>Kṣatriya</s> and a <s>Vaiśya</s> is like that for a Brahmin and a <s>Rājanya</s>.
The sin of theft for a <s>Śūdra</s> is punished eightfold.
For the others, by caste, the penalties increase twofold successively.
When a learned man transgresses, the punishment is heavier.
For taking fruits, green grain, or vegetables, the small fine is five <s>kṛṣṇalas</s>.
When damage is done by cattle, the fault belongs to the owner.
But if a herdsman is connected with that animal, the fault is his.
On a road or in an unfenced field, it belongs to the herdsman and the field-owner.
For a cow, five <s>māṣas</s>.
For a camel or donkey, six.
For a horse or buffalo, ten.
For goats and sheep, two each.
For total destruction, one hundred.

children.text: śiṣṭākaraṇe pratiṣiddhasevāyāṃ ca nityaṃ cailapiṇḍād ūrdhvaṃ svaharaṇam ||
children.translated_text: For not doing what is prescribed by the learned and for resorting to what is forbidden, confiscation of property always applies beyond a garment and a lump of food.

children.text: go'gnyarthe tṛṇamedhān vīrudvanaspatīnāṃ ca puṣpāṇi svavad ādadīta phalāni cāparivṛtānām ||
children.translated_text: For the sake of cows or fire, one may take grass and fuel, and flowers of creepers and trees, as if they were one’s own, and also fruits from those not enclosed.
The lawful interest on a loan is twenty, at five <s>māṣas</s> per month.
Some say it should not go beyond a year.
When the debt has stood for a long time, the principal becomes doubled.
A usufructuary pledge does not increase.
Nor does the debt of one who is willing to pay or whose payment has been obstructed.
There is revolving-period interest.
And there are stipulated interest, bodily-service interest, crest-interest, and enjoyment of a pledge.
A loan in cattle, produce, wool, fields, grain, or draught animals must not exceed fivefold.
Property of one who is neither dull-witted nor a minor, if enjoyed by others for ten years in the owner’s presence, belongs to the enjoyer.
But not when it is enjoyed by learned Brahmins, renunciants, or royal officers.
There is no adverse enjoyment of cattle, land, or women.
Those who share the inheritance should repay the debt.
Suretyship, commercial tolls, liquor, gambling, and fines should not fall upon the sons.
Deposits, pledges, borrowed goods, bought pledges, and lost property are all chargeable to blameless persons only when lost through a man’s fault.

children.text: stenaḥ prakīrṇakeśo musalī rājānam iyāt karmācakṣānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A thief, with hair disheveled and carrying a club, should go to the king, declaring his act.
He is purified by execution or by release.
If the king does not strike him, the king bears the guilt.
There is no bodily punishment for a Brahmin.
If punishment is not carried out, he becomes liable to penance.
An accomplice who acts knowingly is equal to the thief.
So too the receiver, when the property is connected with unrighteousness.
Punishment is imposed after considering the man’s capacity, the offense, its consequences, and knowledge of it.
Or permission is given according to the statement of an assembly of Veda-knowers, according to the statement of an assembly of Veda-knowers.
When there is disagreement, the establishment of truth depends on witnesses.

children.text: bahavaḥ syur aninditāḥ svakarmasu prātyayikā rājñāṃ niṣprītyanabhitāpāś cānyatarasmin ||
children.translated_text: They should be numerous, blameless, trustworthy in their own occupations, and without affection or resentment toward either side before the king.
Even <s>Śūdras</s> may be witnesses.
But a Brahmin is not to be confined on the word of a non-Brahmin, if he is unattached and unbound.
Those not assembled and not questioned should not speak.
If they do not speak, or speak otherwise, they become guilty.
Heaven follows truthful speech; in the opposite case, hell.
Even those who are not formally bound as witnesses must speak.
A declaration made under coercion is not binding.
Nor one spoken in intoxication or negligence.
Fault falls on the witnesses, assessors, king, and agent when the order of <s>dharma</s> is harmed.
Some hold that truth is established by an oath.
For non-Brahmins, that oath should take place in an assembly of gods, the king, and Brahmins.
A witness who lies about small cattle destroys ten.
In matters of cows, horses, men, and land, he destroys ten times as many successively.
Or, in the case of land, everything.
In theft there is hell.
In the case of water, the rule is as for land.
And in sexual intercourse.
For honey and ghee, the rule is as for cattle.
For garments, gold, grain, and sacred knowledge, the rule is as for cows.
For vehicles, the rule is as for horses.
A witness who speaks falsely is to be made to pay maintenance and is to be fined.
There is no fault in speaking an untruth if life depends on it.
But not the life of a worse sinner.
The king, or a Brahmin learned in the śāstra, is the chief judge.
He should appoint a chief judge.
When no surety is available, he should wait for a year.
But in matters connected with cows, draught oxen, women, and procreation, he should act quickly.
And in urgent matters.
In court, truthful speech is weightier than all <s>dharma</s>, truthful speech.
Impurity from a corpse lasts ten nights for <s>sapiṇḍa</s> kinsmen who are not officiating priests, consecrated sacrificers, or students.
For a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, eleven nights.
For a <s>Vaiśya</s>, twelve nights.
Some say half a month.
For a <s>Śūdra</s>, a month.

children.text: tac ced antaḥ punar āpateccheṣeṇa śudhyeran ||
children.translated_text: If that should recur before the end, they are purified by the remaining period.
If it occurs with the night remaining, by two nights.
If it occurs at dawn, by three nights.
For those killed for the sake of cows or Brahmins, immediately after.
And for one killed by the king's anger.
In battle.
And for those who voluntarily die by setting out without food, by weapons, fire, poison, water, hanging, or falling.
The cessation of the funeral piṇḍa offerings is on the seventh or the fifth day.
At a birth also the same rule applies.
For the mother and father, or for the mother alone.
If the embryo miscarries, the impurity lasts as many days and nights as there were months of pregnancy.
Or for three days.
When one hears of it after the tenth day, the impurity lasts a day and a night with the intervening day.
For a non-<s>sapiṇḍa</s> connected by marriage, and for a fellow student.
For one who shared the same brahmacarya, one day.
And for a learned Vedic scholar who has died.
On touching a corpse, there is impurity for ten nights, if the contact was intentional.
For <s>Vaiśyas</s> and <s>Śūdras</s>, the rule has been stated.
Or for women in menstruation.
And for the two preceding classes.
Or for three days.
The same applies in the case of the teacher, his son, his wife, one for whom one sacrifices, and a pupil.

children.text: avaraś ced varṇaḥ pūrvavarṇam upaspṛśet pūrvo vāvaraṃ tatra śavoktam āśaucam ||
children.translated_text: If a lower varṇa touches a higher varṇa, or a higher one touches a lower one, the impurity there is as stated for a corpse.

On contact with one who is fallen, a Caṇḍāla, a woman recently delivered, a menstruating woman, one who has touched a corpse, or one touched by such a person, one is purified by bathing in water with one's clothes on.
And when following a corpse.
And after contact with a dog.
Some say, after whatever has injured one.
The water offering is made by <s>sapiṇḍa</s> kinsmen for one whose tonsure has been performed.
And for their women.
Some say, for those who have been given in marriage.
All should sleep and sit on the ground and live as brahmacārins.
They should not anoint themselves.
They should not eat meat until the offering has been made.
The water rite is performed on the first, third, seventh, and ninth days.
And garments are to be discarded.
But for the lowest classes, at the end.
From the appearance of teeth and the like, by the mother and father.
For a child, one abroad, an ascetic, and non-<s>sapiṇḍas</s>, purification is immediate.
And for kings, because public business would be obstructed.
And for a Brahmin, for the sake of not interrupting Vedic recitation, for the sake of not interrupting Vedic recitation.
Now, the śrāddha.
On the new-moon day one should give to the ancestors.
Or on days beginning with the fifth of the dark fortnight.
Or throughout the whole fortnight, according to one's faith.
When suitable materials, place, and Brahmins are present, the time rule applies.
According to one's ability one should improve the quality, preparation, and prescribed treatment of the food.
One should feed nine, or fewer, in odd numbers.
Or according to one's capacity.
Or learned Vedic scholars endowed with speech, appearance, age, and character.
The gift should first be made to the young men.
Some say, as to the ancestors.
And one should not thereby perform an act of friendship.

children.text: putrābhāve sapiṇḍā mātṛsapiṇḍāḥ śiṣyāś ca dadyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the absence of sons, <s>sapiṇḍas</s>, maternal <s>sapiṇḍas</s>, and pupils should make the offering.
In their absence, the officiating priest and the teacher.
By gifts of sesame, beans, rice, barley, and water, the ancestors are pleased for a month.
By the meats of fish, antelope, ruru deer, hare, tortoise, boar, and ram, for years.
By cow's milk and milk-rice, for twelve years.
By the meat of the vārdhrīṇasa, and by kālaśāka, goat, red goat, and rhinoceros meat mixed with honey, satisfaction is endless.

One should not feed thieves, eunuchs, fallen men, atheists, those who live like them, killers of heroes, husbands of elder sisters married after younger sisters, women, village priests, goat-herds, those who have abandoned the sacred fire, drinkers of liquor, men of bad conduct, false witnesses, or public performers.
An adulterer.
And one to whom that applies.

Nor those who eat from a kuṇḍa, sellers of Soma, house-burners, poisoners, students who have broken their vow, servants of corporations, men who approach forbidden women, violent men, younger brothers married before elder brothers, elder brothers passed over in marriage, those who sacrifice for the unfit or have such sacrifices performed, self-abandoners, men with bad hair, bad nails, black teeth, lepers, sons of remarried women, gamblers, those who sacrifice or have sacrifice performed for improper persons, servants, counterfeiters, husbands of Śūdra women, deformed men, spotted lepers, usurers, merchants, those living by crafts, and those whose habits are bow-playing, instrumental music, beating time, dancing, and singing.
And those divided from their father against his will.
Some include pupils and men of the same gotra.
After three days one may feed
a man of good qualities.

children.text: sadyaḥ śrāddhī śūdrātalpagas tatpurīṣe māsaṃ nayati pitṝn ||
children.translated_text: A man who has just performed a śrāddha and lies on a Śūdra woman's bed carries the ancestors into her excrement for a month.
Therefore on that day he should be celibate.
It is spoiled by the sight of a dog, a Caṇḍāla, or a fallen man.
Therefore one should give it in a screened place.
Or one should scatter sesame seeds around.
Or a purifier of the row may neutralize it.

children.text: paṅktipāvanaḥ ṣaḍaṅgavij jyeṣṭhasāmikas triṇāciketastrimadhus trisuparṇaḥ pañcāgniḥ snātako mantrabrāhmaṇavid dharmajño brahmadeyānusaṃtāna iti ||
children.translated_text: A purifier of the row is one who knows the six Vedāṅgas, one who knows the Jyeṣṭhasāman, one who has performed the triṇāciketa rite, one who knows the trimadhu, one who knows the trisuparṇa, one who maintains the five fires, a snātaka, one who knows the mantras and brāhmaṇas, one who knows dharma, or one descended from recipients of brahmadeya gifts.
The same applies with sacrificial oblations.
At a śrāddha, some exclude each one beginning with those of bad hair.
And the same applies at a śrāddha where no cooked food has been prepared, the same applies.
Beginning with <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, or with <s>Proṣṭhapadī</s>, after the annual opening ceremony, one should study the Vedas.
For four and a half months, or for five months, or through the southern course of the sun.
Living as a brahmacārin, with hair and nails uncut, he should not eat meat.
Or the observance lasts for two months.
One should not recite when, by day, the wind carries dust.
Nor at night when the wind is audible to the ear.
Nor when the sounds of arrows, drums, mṛdaṅgas, pits, or cries of distress are heard.
Nor at the combined howling of dogs, jackals, and donkeys.
Nor when there is red glow, a rainbow, or mist.
And, out of season, when clouds are seen.
When one has urinated or defecated.
At night, at twilight, and in water.
And while it is raining.
Some say, when streams of water flow.
When serving the teacher.
And at the two twilights.
When frightened, riding in a vehicle, lying down, or with feet raised.
In a cremation ground, at the edge of a village, on a great road, and in states of impurity.
When there is a foul smell, in the presence of a corpse, one infamous by day, or a Śūdra.
And after eating, at a belch.
And the Ṛgveda and Yajurveda should not be recited as long as the sound of the Sāmaveda is heard.
Untimely interruptions are thunderbolts, earthquakes, eclipses of Rāhu, and meteors.
Thunder, rain, and lightning, when fires have been kindled, also cause a suspension.
In the rainy season, for the day.
When there is lightning, at night also, after the latter part of the night.
When it begins from the first of the three parts, the whole period is affected.
Some include meteors together with lightning.
Thunder in the afternoon causes suspension.
Also at evening twilight.
At night the whole period is affected from midnight onward.
If it is daytime, so long as there is light.
And when the king who is in one's district has died.
And when people have returned from being away, in relation to one another.
For a day and night in cases of confusion, when the Veda has been placed aside, completion of Vedic study, vomiting, a śrāddha, and eating at a human sacrifice.
And on the new-moon day.
Or for two days.
The full moons of Kārttikī, Phālgunī, and Āṣāḍhī are such occasions.
The three Aṣṭakās cause a suspension for three nights.
Some say this applies to the last one.
On both sides of the annual rite.
All are suspended when rain, lightning, and thunder occur together.
When there is flowing water.
After eating, during a festival.
And, after previous study, for four muhūrtas at night.
Some say this is constant in a city.
An impure man is impure even mentally.
For those engaged in a śrāddha, the occasion is untimely for study.
Even when in contact with one for whom a śrāddha without cooked food has been performed.
And according to each branch of knowledge, those occasions which they remember.
A Brahmin should eat from twice-born men who are approved in their own occupations.
And he may accept gifts from them.

Fuel, water, barley, roots, fruits, honey, what is offered for protection, a bed, a seat, lodging, a vehicle, milk, curds, grain, small fish, priyaṅgu, garlands, a path, and vegetables are not to be refused from anyone.
Other things too may be accepted for maintaining fathers, gods, teachers, and dependants.
And if livelihood is impossible otherwise, from a <s>Śūdra</s>.
Food may be eaten from cattle-keepers, field-ploughers, family associates, agents, and servants.
And from a merchant who is not an artisan.
The following is always uneatable.
Food into which hair or insects have fallen.
Food touched by a menstruating woman or struck by the foot of a black bird.
Food looked at by a killer of an embryo.
Food spoiled in its condition or intention.
Food smelled by a cow.
Fermented sour food by itself, except curds.
Food cooked again.
Stale food, except vegetables, edible roots, fat, meat, and honey.

Food left by an outcast woman, by one who is accused, by one not to be named, by a staff-bearing ascetic, carpenter, cave-dweller, jailer, physician, hunter, fowler, seller of arrows, eater of leavings, or enemy of the group.
Food of those unfit to sit in the line, down to the prāgdurvāla class.
Food from which the useless food, sipping water, rising, and separation have passed away.
Honor should be given to equals and unequals in even and uneven fashion by means of the equal and the non-equal.
And what has not been honored is not to be eaten.
And the milk of a cow within ten days after calving, during the period of birth impurity.
And that of a goat or buffalo as well.

children.text: nityam āvikam apeyam auṣṭram aikaśaphaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Sheep's milk, camel's milk, and that of one-hoofed animals are always not to be drunk.
And the milk of cows called syandinī, yamāsū, and saṃdhinī.
And of one whose calf is dead or absent.
Five-clawed animals are not eaten, except the porcupine, hare, hedgehog, iguana, rhinoceros, and tortoise.
Animals with teeth in both jaws, hairy or woolly creatures, one-hoofed animals, kalaviṅkas, plavas, cakravākas, and haṃsas are forbidden.
Crows, herons, vultures, hawks, aquatic creatures with red feet or beaks, and domestic cocks and pigs are forbidden.
And the cow and the draught ox.
Meat from animals that have fallen into distress, sunk down, or died uselessly is forbidden.
Sprouts, kyākula, garlic, and resins from trees are forbidden.
Red-colored and cut-off things are forbidden.
The nicuda, arubaka, crane, parrot, madgu, ṭiṭṭibha, māndhāla, and night-roaming creatures are not to be eaten.
Birds that peck, scratch, or have webbed feet are edible.
And fish, if they are not deformed.
And animals may be killed for the sake of <s>dharma</s>.
After sprinkling them, one may eat those killed by predators, those without visible defect, and those praised by reliable speech; one may eat them.
A woman is not independent in matters of <s>dharma</s>.
She should not transgress her husband.
She should be restrained in speech, sight, and action.
A woman without a husband who desires offspring may obtain it from her brother-in-law.
Once she has borne a son by authority of the elders, she should not pass beyond the season.
She may obtain it from those connected by piṇḍa, gotra, or seer-lineage, or merely by birth relation.
Some say: not from anyone other than the brother-in-law.
Not beyond a second man.
The child belongs to the begetter.
Or, by agreement, to another.
And, while the husband is alive, it belongs to the owner of the field.
From another man, it belongs to that other.
Or to both.
But because of protection, it belongs to the husband alone.
Intercourse is permitted when the report is heard.
But if he has become a renunciant, she must desist, because of attachment.
For a Brahmin, twelve years are allowed in connection with Vedic study.
Likewise, when there is an elder brother, a younger one should wait in taking a wife and kindling the sacred fire.
Some say six years.

children.text: trīn kumāryṛtūn atītya svayaṃ yujyetāninditenotsṛjya pitryān alaṃkārān ||
children.translated_text: After three menstrual periods of a maiden have passed, she may choose for herself a blameless man, abandoning the ornaments given by her father.
Giving her in marriage should be before menstruation.
One who does not give her is at fault.
Some say before she assumes clothing.
Taking wealth for the accomplishment of marriage, and in a connection governed by the dharma-system, may be from a <s>Śūdra</s>.
In other cases too, from a <s>Śūdra</s> who has much cattle and does low work.
From one who has a hundred cows and has not established the sacred fire.
And from one who has a thousand cows and has not drunk soma.
And he should not consume the seventh part, in order to avoid accumulation.
Even from those whose occupations are not inferior.
When questioned by the king, he should declare it.
For the king must maintain him, if he is endowed with learning and character.
When the dharma-system is oppressed, there is fault in not doing this, fault indeed.
The dharma of the social classes and the dharma of the life-stages have been stated.

children.text: atha khalvayaṃ puruṣo yāpyena karmaṇā lipyate yathaitad ayājyayājanam abhakṣyabhakṣaṇam avadyavadanaṃ śiṣṭasyākriyā pratiṣiddhasevanam iti ||
children.translated_text: Now this person is tainted by a blameworthy act, such as sacrificing for one for whom he should not sacrifice, eating what should not be eaten, speaking what is blameworthy, failing to do what the learned do, or practicing what is forbidden.

children.text: tatra prāyaścittaṃ kuryāt na kuryād iti mīmāṃsante ||
children.translated_text: In such a case they deliberate whether he should perform a penance or should not perform one.
They say that he should not perform one.
For an act is not destroyed.
Another view says that he should perform one.
For it is known that after sacrificing with a punaḥstoma, they return again to the soma-pressing.
And after sacrificing with the vrātyastomas.

children.text: tarati sarvaṃ pāpmānaṃ tarati brahmahatyāṃ yo 'śvamedhena yajate ||
children.translated_text: He crosses beyond every evil; he crosses beyond the killing of a Brahmin, who sacrifices with the horse-sacrifice.
And it is said that one accused should be made to sacrifice with the Agniṣṭut rite.

children.text: tasya niṣkrayaṇāni japas tapo homa upavāso dānam ||
children.translated_text: The means of redeeming him are muttering, austerity, oblation, fasting, and giving.

children.text: upaniṣado vedāntaḥ sarvacchandaḥsu saṃhitā madhūnyaghamarṣaṇam atharvaśiro rudrāḥ puruṣasūktaṃ rājatarauhiṇe sāmanībṛhadrathantare puruṣagatir mahānāmnyo mahāvairājaṃ mahādivākīrtyaṃ jyeṣṭhasāmnām anyatamad bahiṣpavamānaṃ kūṣmāṇḍāni pāvamānyaḥ sāvitrī ceti pāvamānāni ||
children.translated_text: The purifying recitations are these: the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, the <s>Vedānta</s>, the collection in all meters, the <s>Madhu</s> hymns, the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s>, the <s>Atharvaśiras</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, the <s>Rājatarauhiṇa</s> chants, the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s>, the <s>Puruṣagati</s>, the <s>Mahānāmnīs</s>, the <s>Mahāvairāja</s>, the <s>Mahādivākīrtya</s>, any one of the <s>Jyeṣṭhasāmans</s>, the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s>, the <s>Kūṣmāṇḍas</s>, the <s>Pāvamānīs</s>, and the <s>Sāvitrī</s>.

children.text: payovratatā śākabhakṣatā phalabhakṣatā prasṛtayāvako hiraṇyaprāśanaṃ ghṛtaprāśanaṃ somapānam itimedhyāni ||
children.translated_text: Living on milk, living on vegetables, living on fruits, barley gruel by handfuls, swallowing gold, swallowing ghee, and drinking soma are the purifying consumptions.

children.text: sarve śiloccayāḥ sarvāḥ sravantyaḥ puṇyā hradāstīrthāny ṛṣinivāsā goṣṭhapariskandhā iti deśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All heaps of stones, all flowing rivers, holy ponds, sacred fords, dwellings of seers, and cattle-pen enclosures are the places.

children.text: brahmacaryaṃ satyavacanaṃ savaneṣūdakopasparśanam ārdravastratādhaḥśāyitānāśaka iti tapāṃsi ||
children.translated_text: Celibacy, speaking truth, touching water at the pressings, wearing wet clothes, sleeping on the ground, and fasting are the austerities.

children.text: hiraṇyaṃ gaur vāso 'śvo bhūmis tilā ghṛtam annam iti deyānīti ||
children.translated_text: Gold, a cow, a garment, a horse, land, sesame, ghee, and food are the things to be given.

children.text: saṃvatsaraḥ ṣaṇmāsāś catvāras trayo vā dvau vaikaś caturviṃśatyaho dvādaśāhaḥ ṣaḍahas tryaho 'horātra iti kālāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A year, six months, four, three, or two months, one month, twenty-four days, twelve days, six days, three days, and a day and night are the periods.
In the absence of a specific prescription, these very things should be performed optionally.
For grave offenses, grave penances; for light offenses, light ones.
The <s>kṛcchra</s>, the <s>atikṛcchra</s>, and the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> are expiations for all sins.

children.text: tyajet pitaraṃ rājaghātakaṃ śūdrayājakaṃ śūdrārthayājakaṃ vedaviplāvakaṃ bhrūṇahanaṃ yaś cāntyāvasāyibhiḥ saha saṃvased antyāvasāyinyāṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: One should abandon a father who kills a king, sacrifices for <s>Śūdras</s>, sacrifices for the benefit of <s>Śūdras</s>, corrupts the Veda, kills an embryo, or who lives together with outcastes or with an outcaste woman.

children.text: tasya vidyāgurūn yonisaṃbandhāṃś ca saṃnipātya sarvāṇy udakādīni pretakāryāṇi kuryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: His teachers in sacred learning and his blood relations should assemble and perform for him all the rites for the dead, beginning with the water offering.
And they should overturn his vessel.

children.text: dāsaḥ karmakaro vāvakarād amedhyapātram ānīya dāsīghaṭāt pūrayitvā dakṣiṇāmukho yadā viparyasyed amukam anudakaṃ karomi iti nāmagrāham ||
children.translated_text: A slave or hired servant, bringing an impure vessel from a refuse heap and filling it from a slave woman's water-pot, should face south and overturn it, saying by name, 'I make so-and-so without water.'
All of them, wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder and with their topknots loosened, should touch him afterward.
The teachers in sacred learning and the blood relations should look on.
After touching water, they enter the village.

children.text: ata uttaraṃ tena sambhāṣya tiṣṭhed ekarātraṃ japansāvitrīm ajñānapūrvam ||
children.translated_text: After that, if one converses with him unknowingly, one should stand for one night muttering the <s>Sāvitrī</s>.
If knowingly, for three nights.

children.text: yas tu prāyaścittena śudhyet tasmiñ śuddhe śātakumbhamayaṃ pātraṃ puṇyatamāddhradāt pūrayitvā sravantībhyo vā tata enam apa upasparśayeyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: But one who can be purified by penance, when he has become pure, they should fill a golden vessel from the holiest pond, or from flowing waters, and then make him touch the water.

children.text: athāsmai tatpātram dadyus tatapratigṛhya japecchāntā dyauḥ śāntā pṛthivī śāntaṃ śivam antarikṣaṃ yo rocanastābhamam gṛhṇāmīti ||
children.translated_text: Then they should give that vessel to him; after receiving it he should mutter, 'Peaceful is heaven, peaceful is earth, peaceful and auspicious is the midspace; I take what has the radiance.'

children.text: etair yajurbhiḥ pāvamānībhis taratsamandībhiḥ kūṣmāṇḍaiś cājyaṃ juhuyāddhiraṇyaṃ brāhmaṇāya dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: With these <s>yajus</s> formulas, with the <s>Pāvamānī</s> verses, with the <s>Taratsamandī</s> verses, and with the <s>Kūṣmāṇḍas</s>, he should offer ghee and give gold to a Brahmin.
And to his teacher.

children.text: yasya tu prāṇāntikaṃ prāyaścittaṃ sa mṛtaḥ śudhyet ||
children.translated_text: But one whose expiation lasts until the end of life is purified when dead.

children.text: sarvāṇy eva tasmin udakādīni pretakarmāṇi kuryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: For him they should perform all the rites for the dead, beginning with the water offering.
This same water of pacification is used in all secondary sins, in all secondary sins.

Killers of Brahmins, drinkers of liquor, violators of a teacher's bed, offenders against mother, father, or blood relations, thieves of gold, atheists, those habituated to censured acts, fallen persons who must not be abandoned, and abandoners of fallen persons are fallen.
And so are those who cause association with sins.
And one who associates with them for a year.
Falling is the loss of the rites belonging to the twice-born.
And likewise failure in the next world.
Some call that hell.
The first three are not to be explicitly named, according to some.
Some say that among women, intercourse with one who is not the teacher's wife does not cause falling.
A woman falls through killing an embryo and through service to a man of lower caste.

children.text: kauṭasākṣyaṃ rājagāmi paiśunam guror anṛtābhiśaṃsanaṃ mahāpātakasamāni ||
children.translated_text: False testimony, carrying tales to the king, slander, and falsely accusing a teacher are equal to the great sins.

Before <s>Durvāla</s>, among those unfit for the line, there is a secondary sin in the case of a cow-killer, a Brahmin-killer, one merely doing the same, an unchaste student, a fallen man, and one who has lost the <s>Sāvitrī</s>.

children.text: ajñānād anadhyāpanād ṛtvigācāryau patanīyasevāyāṃ ca heyau ||
children.translated_text: Through ignorance, through not teaching, and in service to one who causes falling, the officiating priest and the teacher are to be abandoned.
Except through abandonment, he falls.
And, according to some, also the receiver of his gifts.
There is never non-maintenance of mother and father.
But they should not share the inheritance.
In falsely accusing a Brahmin, the fault is just as great.
Twice as great in the case of an innocent man.
And in injuring a weak person, if one is able to release him.
Threatening an angered Brahmin with a raised weapon keeps one from heaven for a hundred years.
For striking him, for a thousand years.
If blood is seen, for as many years as he would gather dust after it has flowed out.
This is the expiation.
For a killer of a Brahmin, there is throwing oneself into the fire after three times proclaiming the act.
Or he may be a target in battle for weapon-bearing men.

children.text: khaṭvāṅgakapālapāṇir vā dvādaśa saṃvatsarān brahmacārī bhaikṣāya grāmaṃ praviśet karmācakṣāṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, holding a staff with a skull at its top and a skull in his hand, he should live as a celibate for twelve years and enter a village for alms, declaring his deed.
He should move off the road at the sight of an <s>Ārya</s>.
Wandering without sitting or lying down, and touching water at the pressings, he becomes pure.
Or by saving the life of a Brahmin for that reason.
In the case of loss of property, he is restored after making restitution at least threefold.
Or at the final bath of a horse-sacrifice.
Even at another's sacrifice, if it ends with an <s>Agniṣṭut</s>.
If he has been commissioned in the killing of a Brahmin, even without himself killing him.
And the same applies in the case of women of the <s>Ātreya</s> line.
And when the embryo is not yet known.

children.text: rājanyavadhe ṣaḍvārṣikaṃ prākṛtaṃ brahmacaryamṛṣabhaikasahasrāś ca gā dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: For killing a <s>Rājanya</s>, the ordinary six-year chastity-vow is prescribed, and he should give one thousand cows together with one bull.

children.text: vaiśye tu traivārṣikam ṛṣabhaikaśatāś ca gā dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: But for a <s>Vaiśya</s>, it is a three-year vow, and he should give one hundred cows together with one bull.

children.text: śūdre saṃvatsaram ṛṣabhaikādaśāś ca gā dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: For a <s>Śūdra</s>, it is one year, and he should give eleven cows together with one bull.
And the same applies to a woman who is not of the <s>Ātreya</s> line.
And for killing a cow, the rule is as for a <s>Vaiśya</s>.
And in cases of violence to a frog, mongoose, crow, bimbada, rat, dog, and snake.
After killing a thousand creatures that have bones.
And for boneless creatures, when the load of a cart has been killed.
Or, in the case of creatures with bones, he should give something for each one.
For killing a eunuch, a load of straw and a māṣa of lead are due.
For a boar, a pot of ghee.
For a snake, an iron staff.
For a <s>brahmabandhu</s> woman who is a wanderer, a blue garment.
For a courtesan, something.
For unlawful taking of a bed, food, or wealth, and for killing, separate years are prescribed.
Two years for another man's wife.
Three years for the wife of a learned Brahmin.
And in the case of acquiring property, relinquishment is prescribed.
Or he should restore it to its proper place.
If he has used a forbidden mantra, the penalty is one thousand recitations, if it is a Vedic formula.
The same applies to extinguishing the sacred fire, rejecting it, and minor sins.

children.text: strī yāticāriṇī guptā piṇḍaṃ tu labheta ||
children.translated_text: A woman who has gone astray, if kept under guard, should nevertheless receive food.

children.text: amānuṣīṣu govarjaṃ strīkṛte kūṣmāṇḍair ghṛtahomo ghṛtahomaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In cases involving non-human females, except for a cow, when the act is treated as with a woman, there is a ghee oblation with the <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> verses; a ghee oblation.

children.text: surāpasya brāhmaṇasyoṣṇām āsiñceyuḥ surām āsye mṛtaḥ śudhyet ||
children.translated_text: For a Brahmin who has drunk liquor, they should pour hot liquor into his mouth; dead, he is purified.

children.text: amatyā pāne payo ghṛtam udakaṃ vāyuṃ prati tryahaṃ taptāni sa kṛcchras tato 'sya saṃskāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: For drinking it unknowingly, he should consume heated milk, ghee, water, and air for three days in succession; this is a <s>kṛcchra</s> penance, and after that comes his reinitiation.
The same applies to swallowing urine, feces, or semen.
And to swallowing part of a wild animal, camel, or donkey.
And of a village fowl or pig.
On smelling the odor of a liquor-drinker, there should be breath-controls and drinking of ghee.
And for one bitten by the preceding animals.
One who has violated his teacher's bed should lie on a heated iron bed.
Or he should embrace a heated metal image.

children.text: liṅgaṃ vā savṛṣaṇam utkṛtya añjalāv ādhāya dakṣiṇāpratīcīṃ vrajed ajihmam ā śarīranipātāt ||
children.translated_text: Or, cutting off his penis together with the testicles, placing them in his joined hands, he should go straight toward the southwest until his body falls.
Dead, he is purified.
With his friend's wife, a woman of the same womb, a woman of the same gotra, a pupil's wife, a daughter-in-law, or a cow, the sin is equal to violating the teacher's bed.
Some say it is an inferior offense.

children.text: śvabhir ādayed rājā nihīnavarṇagamane striyaṃ prakāśam ||
children.translated_text: The king should have a woman who has intercourse with a man of lower caste publicly torn by dogs.
He should have the man killed.
Or the penalty is as stated before.
One who has spilled semen should sacrifice to <s>Nirṛti</s> at a crossroads with a donkey.

children.text: tasyājinam ūrdhvavālaṃ paridhāya lohitapatraḥ saptagṛhān bhakṣaṃ caretkarmācakṣāṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Wearing its hide with the hair turned upward, carrying a red vessel, he should go for alms at seven houses, declaring his deed.
He is purified after a year.

children.text: retaḥskandane bhaye roge svapne 'gnīndhanabhaikṣacaraṇāni saptarātram akṛtvājyahomaḥ samidho vāretasyābhyām ||
children.translated_text: For emission of semen through fear, illness, or a dream, after failing for seven nights to tend the fires and go for alms, he should make a ghee oblation, or offer fuel-sticks with the two verses concerning semen.

children.text: sūryābhyudito brahmacārī tiṣṭhed aharabhuñjāno 'bhyastamitaś ca rātriṃ japan sāvitrīm ||
children.translated_text: A celibate student over whom the sun has risen should stand through the day without eating, and if the sun has set over him, through the night, reciting the <s>Sāvitrī</s>.

children.text: aśuciṃ dṛṣṭvā ādityam īkṣeta prāṇāyāmaṃ kṛtvā ||
children.translated_text: After seeing something impure, he should look at the sun, having performed breath-control.
For eating forbidden food or swallowing something impure, he must reach a state free from excrement.
At minimum, he should go without food for three nights.

children.text: saptarātraṃ vā svayaṃ śīrṇāny upabhuñjānaḥ phalāny anatikrāman ||
children.translated_text: Or for seven nights he may subsist on fruits that have fallen by themselves, without transgressing that rule.
Before eating five-nailed animals, there should be vomiting and drinking of ghee.
For abuse, falsehood, and injury, the highest austerity is three nights.
For a truthful utterance, there is an oblation with the <s>Vāruṇī</s> and <s>Mānavī</s> verses.
Some say there is no fault in an untruth in connection with marriage, sexual intercourse, joking, and distress.
But certainly not in matters concerning the teacher.

children.text: sapta puruṣānitaś ca parataś ca hanti manasāpiguror anṛtaṃ vadann alpeṣv apy artheṣu ||
children.translated_text: One who speaks falsely to his teacher, even mentally and even in small matters, destroys seven generations before and after him.
For intercourse with a woman of the lowest settlement, the penance is a year-long <s>kṛcchra</s>.
If it was unknowingly, twelve nights.
For intercourse with a menstruating woman, three nights.
A secret expiation is for one whose offense is not publicly known.

children.text: caturṛcaṃ taratsamandīty apsu japed apratigrāhyaṃ pratijighṛkṣan pratigṛhya vā ||
children.translated_text: When desiring to accept, or after accepting, what should not be accepted, he should recite in water the four verses beginning <s>taratsamandī</s>.
When desiring to eat what should not be eaten, he should scatter it on the earth.
Some say that after intercourse at a forbidden season, purification comes from touching water.
The same applies with women.

children.text: payovrato vā daśarātraṃ ghṛtena dvitīyam adbhistṛtīyaṃ divādiṣvekabhaktiko jalaklinnavāsā lomāni nakhāni tvacaṃ māṃsaṃ śoṇitaṃ snāyvasthi majjānam iti homā ātmano mukhe mṛtyor āsye juhomītyantataḥ sarveṣāṃ prāyaścittaṃ bhrūṇahatyāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or, observing a milk-vow for ten nights, then a second vow with ghee, a third with water, eating once by day and so on, wearing clothes wet with water, he offers oblations into his own mouth with the formulas 'hairs, nails, skin, flesh, blood, sinews, bones, marrow,' and finally, 'I offer into the mouth of death'; this is the expiation for all of them, including embryo-killing.
Now there is another.
The rule has been stated.

children.text: agne tvaṃ pārayeti mahāvyāhṛtibhirjuhuyāt kūṣmāṇḍaiś cājyam ||
children.translated_text: He should offer ghee with the great vyāhṛtis and the formula 'Agni, carry me across,' and also with the <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> verses.

children.text: tadvrata eva vā brahmahatyāsurāpānasteyagurutalpeṣu prāṇāyāmais tānto 'ghamarṣaṇaṃ japan samam aśvamedhāvabhṛthenedaṃ ca prāyaścittam ||
children.translated_text: Or, under that same vow, for Brahmin-killing, liquor-drinking, theft, and violation of the teacher's bed, one who is worn out by breath-controls and recites the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> obtains the same result as the final bath of a horse-sacrifice; and this too is an expiation.
Or by repeating the <s>Sāvitrī</s> a thousand times, one purifies oneself even here.
Or, by repeating the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> three times while standing in water, one is freed from all sins.
They say this: into how many deities does one who has spilled semen enter?

children.text: marutaḥ prāṇenendre balena bṛhaspatiṃ brahmavarcasenāgnim evetareṇa sarveṇeti ||
children.translated_text: Into the <s>Maruts</s> with breath, into <s>Indra</s> with strength, into <s>Bṛhaspati</s> with sacred brilliance, and into <s>Agni</s> with all the rest.

children.text: so 'māvāsyāyāṃ niśyagnim upasamādhāya prāyaś cittājyāhutīr juhoti ||
children.translated_text: On the night of the new moon, having kindled the fire, he offers ghee oblations of expiation.
"I am overcome by desire, I am overcome; svāhā to the desire for desire."

children.text: kāmābhidugdho 'smi abhidugdho 'smi kāmakāmāya svāheti samidham ādhāya anuparyukṣya yajñavāstu kṛtvopotthāya samāsiñcatu ityetayā trir upatiṣṭheta ||
children.translated_text: Having placed on the fire a fuel-stick with, "I am milked by desire, I am milked; svāhā to the desire for desire," having sprinkled around and made it a sacrificial place, he should rise and worship three times with the formula, "May he pour together."

children.text: traya ime lokā eṣāṃ lokānām abhijityā abhikrāntyeti ||
children.translated_text: "These are the three worlds; for the conquest of these worlds, for the stepping over them," thus.
