children.text: etad evaikeṣām karmādhikṛtya yo 'prayata iva syāt sa itthaṃ juhuyād ittham anumantrayeta varo dakṣiṇeti prāyaścittamaviśeṣāt ||
children.translated_text: Some prescribe this same rite with reference to ritual action: if a man should be, as it were, impure, he should sacrifice in this way and recite the accompanying formula in this way; the fee is a boon. Because there is no distinction, it is an expiation.

children.text: anārjavapaiśunapratiṣiddhācārān ādyaprāśaneṣu śūdrāyāṃ ca retaḥ siktvā ayonau ca doṣavati ca karmaṇy api saṃdhipūrve 'bliṅgābhir apa upaspṛśed vāruṇībhir anyair vā pavitraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For crookedness, tale-bearing, forbidden conduct, at first eatings, after emitting semen in a <s>Śūdra</s> woman, in an improper place, or even in a faulty ritual act preceded by a saṃdhi, he should touch water with verses not marked by that sign, with <s>Vāruṇī</s> verses or other purifying verses.
For forbidden offenses of speech and mind, the vyāhṛtis ending with the fivefold "truth" are used.

children.text: sarvāsv apo vācāmed ahaś ca mādityāś ca punātviti prātā rātriś ca mā varuṇaś ca punātviti sāyam ||
children.translated_text: In all cases there is water: in the morning with, "May the lord of speech, the day, and the <s>Ādityas</s> purify me," and in the evening with, "May the night and <s>Varuṇa</s> purify me."

children.text: aṣṭo vā samidha ādadhyād devakṛtasyeti hutvaiva sarvasmād enaso mucyate ||
children.translated_text: Or he should lay on eight fuel-sticks; after offering with "for what has been done by the gods," he is freed from every sin.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the kṛcchras.

children.text: haviṣyān prātarāśān bhuktvā tisro rātrīr nāśnīyāt ||
children.translated_text: After eating sacrificial food as his morning meal, he should not eat for three nights.
Then for the next three-day period he should eat at night.
Then for the next three-day period he should ask nothing from anyone.
Then for the next three-day period he should fast.
If he desires speed, he should stand by day and sit by night.
He should speak the truth.
He should not converse with ignoble people.
He should constantly employ the <s>Raurava</s> and <s>Yaudhājapa</s> recitations.

children.text: anusavanam udakopasparśanam āpo hi ṣṭheti tisṛbhiḥ pavitravatībhir mārjayīta hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayaḥ pāvakā ityaṣṭābhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: At each pressing-time he should touch water, and he should cleanse himself with the three purifying verses beginning "The waters indeed are you," and with the eight verses beginning "Golden-colored, pure, purifying."
Then comes the water-libation.

children.text: namo 'hamāya mohamāya maṃhamāya dhanvate tāpasāya punarvasave namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Homage to <s>Ahamā</s>, to <s>Mohamā</s>, to <s>Maṃhamā</s>, to the archer, to the ascetic, to <s>Punarvasu</s>; homage."
"Homage to <s>Mauñjyā</s>, to <s>Urvī</s>, to <s>Vasuvinda</s>, to <s>Sārvavinda</s>; homage."

children.text: namaḥ pārāya supārāya mahāpārāya vārayiṣṇave namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Homage to the further shore, to the good further shore, to the great further shore, to the restrainer; homage."

children.text: namo rudrāya paśupataye mahate devāya tryambakāyaikacarāyādhipataye harāya śarvāyeśānāyogrāya vajriṇe ghṛṇine kapardine namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Homage to <s>Rudra</s>, to <s>Paśupati</s>, to the great god, to the three-eyed one, to the solitary wanderer, to the overlord, to <s>Hara</s>, to <s>Śarva</s>, to <s>Īśāna</s>, to the fierce one, to the thunderbolt-bearer, to the glowing one, to the matted-haired one; homage."
"Homage to <s>Sūrya</s>, to <s>Āditya</s>; homage."
"Homage to the blue-necked one, to the white-throated one; homage."
"Homage to the black one, to the tawny one; homage."
"Homage to the eldest, to the ancient, to <s>Indra</s>, to the yellow-haired one, to the one whose seed is raised upward; homage."

children.text: namaḥ satyāya pāvakāya pāvakavarṇāya kāmāya kāmarūpiṇe namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Homage to the true one, to the purifying one, to the one of purifying color, to desire, to the one who takes the form of desire; homage."
"Homage to the blazing one, to the one of blazing form; homage."
"Homage to the sharp one, to the one of sharp form; homage."

children.text: namaḥ sobhyāya supuruṣāya mahāpuruṣāya madhyamapuruṣāyottamapuruṣāya brahmacāriṇe namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Homage to the gracious one, to the good person, to the great person, to the middle person, to the highest person, to the brahmacārin; homage."
"Homage to the one with the moon on his forehead, to the one clothed in a hide; homage."
This same is the worship of the sun.
These same are the ghee-offerings.

children.text: dvādaśarātrasyānte caruṃ śrapayitvā etābhyo devatābhyo juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: At the end of twelve nights, after cooking a caru offering, he should sacrifice to these deities.

children.text: agnaye svāhā somāya svāhāgniṣomābhyām indrāgnibhyām indrāya viśvebhyo devebhyo brahmaṇe prajāpataye 'gnaye sviṣṭakṛta iti ||
children.translated_text: "Svāhā to <s>Agni</s>, svāhā to <s>Soma</s>, to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, to <s>Indra</s>, to all the gods, to <s>Brahman</s>, to <s>Prajāpati</s>, to <s>Agni</s> the maker of the well-offered," thus.
Then comes the satisfaction of Brahmins.
By this same rule the atikṛcchra has been explained.
He should eat only as much as he would take once.
The third form is water as food; that is the kṛcchrātikṛcchra.

children.text: prathamaṃ caritvā śuciḥ pūtaḥ karmaṇyo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the first, he becomes clean, purified, and fit for ritual action.

children.text: dvitīyaṃ caritvā yatkiṃcid anyan mahāpātakebhyaḥ pāpaṃ kurute tasmāt pramucyate ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the second, he is released from whatever sin he commits other than the great sins.
Having performed the third, he is freed from every sin.

children.text: athaitāṃs trīn kṛcchrāṃś caritvā sarveṣu vedeṣu snāto bhavati sarvair devair jñāto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: And after performing these three kṛcchras, he becomes one who has bathed in all the Vedas and one known by all the gods.
And so too is one who knows this.
Now, therefore, the cāndrāyaṇa.
Its procedure has been stated under the kṛcchra.
He should shave and observe the vow.
On the following full-moon day he should fast.

children.text: āpyāyasva saṃ te payāṃsi navonava iti caitābhis tarpaṇam ājyahomo haviṣaś cānumantraṇamupasthānaṃ candramasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With these formulas, beginning "Increase; let your fluids come together" and "new and new," there are the libation, the ghee-offering, the consecration of the sacrificial food, and the worship of the moon.
He should offer with the four verses beginning "Whatever offense against the gods, O gods."
And at the end, with fuel-sticks, using "for what has been done by the gods."

children.text: oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svas tapaḥ satyaṃ yaśaḥ śrīr ūrgiḍaujas tejo varcaḥ puruṣo dharmaḥ śiva ityetair grāsānumantraṇaṃ pratimantraṃ manasā ||
children.translated_text: With these formulas, "oṃ, earth, atmosphere, heaven, heat, truth, fame, prosperity, strength, power, vigor, brilliance, radiance, person, <s>dharma</s>, auspiciousness," he should consecrate each morsel mentally, mantra by mantra.
Or he may use "homage, svāhā" for all of them.
The size of a morsel is what does not distort the mouth.
Caru, alms-food, roasted flour, broken grain, yāvaka, vegetables, milk, curds, ghee, roots, fruits, and water are sacrificial foods, each later one being more commended than the preceding.
On the full-moon day, after eating fifteen morsels, he should eat during the waning fortnight with one less each day.
On the new-moon day, after fasting, he should eat during the waxing fortnight with one more each day.
Some prescribe the reverse.
Thus the cāndrāyaṇa lasts a month.

children.text: evam āptvā vipāpo vipāpmā sarvam eno hanti ||
children.translated_text: Having completed it in this way, sinless and free from evil, he destroys every sin.

children.text: dvitīyam āptvā daśa pūrvān daśa parān ātmānaṃ caikaviṃśaṃ paṅktiṃ ca punāti ||
children.translated_text: Having completed it a second time, he purifies ten ancestors, ten descendants, himself as the twenty-first, and the row.

children.text: saṃvatsaraṃ cāptvā candramasaḥ salokatām āpnoti salokatām āpnoti ||
children.translated_text: And after attaining a year, he obtains residence in the same world as the moon; he obtains residence in the same world.
After the father, the sons should divide the inheritance.
When the mother's menstruation has ceased, if she is alive and wishes it, they should divide.
Or the first-born may take the whole property and support the others as a father would.
But in partition there is an increase of <s>dharma</s> (normative merit).

children.text: viṃśatibhāgo jyeṣṭhasya mithunam ubhayatodadyukto ratho govṛṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The eldest receives a twentieth share, a pair of animals, a chariot yoked on both sides, and a cow-bull.
If there are several, the middle son receives one that is one-eyed, lame, hornless, or of defective color.

children.text: avir dhānyāyasī gṛhamano yuktaṃ catuṣpādaṃ caikaikaṃ yavīyasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A sheep, grain, iron, a house-furnishing, and one serviceable quadruped each belong to the youngest.
The remainder is equal shares.

children.text: ekaikaṃ vā dhanarūpaṃ kāmyaṃ pūrvaḥ pūrvo labhate ||
children.translated_text: Or, in order, each elder one receives one desired item of wealth.
Among cattle, a set of ten is so treated.
But not among one-hoofed animals and bipeds.
An extra bull belongs to the eldest.
Sixteen bulls belong to the eldest's son.
Or the younger sons share equally with the eldest's son.
Or, according to each mother, there is a special share within each one's own class.

children.text: pitotsṛjet putrikāṃ anapatyo 'gniṃ prajāpatiṃ ceṣṭvāsmadartham apatyam iti saṃvādya ||
children.translated_text: A father without a son may appoint a daughter as a <s>putrikā</s>, after sacrificing to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s> and making an agreement, saying, 'A child for my sake.'
Some hold that she is a <s>putrikā</s> merely by intention.
Because of such uncertainty, one should not marry a girl who has no brother.
The relations connected by funeral offerings, gotra, and seers divide the inheritance of a man who has a wife but no offspring.
Or he may seek seed.
A son begotten by another while there is a brother-in-law has no share.
Women's property belongs to daughters who are unmarried and not yet established.
After the mother, the bride-price of a sister belongs to the full brothers.
And some say it belongs even before that.
The division of those deceased without reunion belongs to the eldest.
When one who had reunited dies, the reunited co-sharer takes the inheritance.
A son born after partition receives only the paternal property.

children.text: svayam arjitam avaidyebhyo vaidyaḥ kāmaṃ na dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: A learned man need not, if he wishes, give his self-acquired property to the unlearned.
The unlearned should divide it equally.
Sons who are legitimate, field-born, given, made, secretly born, and abandoned are heirs to the inheritance.
The maiden's son, the son of a pregnant bride, the son of a remarried woman, the appointed daughter's son, the self-given son, and the purchased son share the gotra.
In the absence of the legitimate and the following sons, they receive a fourth share.
For a Brahmin, a son by a Kshatriya woman, if eldest and endowed with virtues, receives an equal share.
The rest is without the eldest's special share.
When there is a combination of sons by Kshatriya and Vaiśya wives, the rule is as with a son by a Brahmin wife.
If the father is a Kshatriya, this applies accordingly.
Even a son by a Śūdra woman, if the man has no offspring and the son is obedient, receives a means of livelihood according to the rule for a resident pupil.
Some say that even a son of the same caste does not inherit if his conduct is improper.
Learned Vedic Brahmins should divide the inheritance of a Brahmin who has no offspring.
For others, the king does so.
The dull-witted and the impotent must be supported.
The offspring of a dull-witted man is entitled to a share.
For women of inverse-caste unions, the rule is as for the son by a Śūdra woman.
There is no division of water, means of subsistence and security, prepared food, and the like.
Nor of women when they are jointly connected.

children.text: anājñāte daśāvaraiḥ śiṣṭair ūhavidbhir alubdhaiḥ praśastaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: When the rule is not known, what is approved by at least ten disciplined men, skilled in reasoning and free from greed, should be done.

children.text: catvāraś caturṇāṃ pāragā vedānāṃ prāg uttamāttraya āśramiṇaḥ pṛthag dharmavidas traya etān daśāvarān pariṣadityācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: They call these a council of at least ten: four men who have mastered the four Vedas, then three men, each in a different āśrama, before the last group, and three who know <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: asambhave tveteṣāṃ śrotriyo vedavicchiṣṭo vipratipattau yad āha ||
children.translated_text: But if these are not available, then in a disputed matter what a learned, disciplined Vedic scholar says is authoritative.
For this person lacks independent authority in matters involving injury and favor toward beings.

children.text: dharmiṇāṃ viśeṣeṇa svargaṃ lokaṃ dharmavid āpnoti jñānābhiniveśābhyām ||
children.translated_text: A knower of <s>dharma</s>, especially among the righteous, obtains the heavenly world through knowledge and steadfast application.
Thus <s>dharma</s>; <s>dharma</s>.
